nodes.label: docs/canon/REVIEW_REGISTER.md — the pile, one row per agent-written document, every row `unreviewed`. Cuts the material by file; REVIEW_WORKLIST.md cuts the same pile by claim. The register appears in its own table and holds the same status as everything listed in it

How to read the register's columns: "What it claims to be" is the file's own first heading copied mechanically — a self-description, not a verdict. "Last written" is the filesystem last-modified date, not authorship date; for committed files `git log --follow` is the better answer. "Status" is `unreviewed` everywhere — nothing in this project has been reviewed by the user. "Evidence pointers found" is a mechanical scan for citation markers ([CHAT]/[DOC] quote tags, git refs, v3/output/ run dirs, corpus references, docs/canon/ references) and reports that pointers exist, not that they support the claims; `none found` means the file asserts without pointing anywhere

The register's eleven sections: 1 docs/canon documents and the review apparatus (10 files); 2 docs/canon/raw records and corpus (6 records + 6 corpus files); 3 root and v3 documents (CLAUDE.md, README.md, docs/ENVIRONMENT.md, v3/CONSTANTS.md, v3/README.md, v3/artefact/DESIGN.md, v3/artefact/MODEL_CONTRACTS.md, v3/artefact/data/README.md, v3/output/DATA_README.md); 4 state docs (5 in-repo + 11 on the OneDrive state-transfer folder); 5 live laptop memory (25 files); 6 desktop memory copy (53 files); 7 laptop memory copy (32 files); 8 agent definitions (10); 9 other agent-written tree material; 10 legacy worktrees (57 docs); 11 what the register does not cover

The docs/canon documents are in the pile on the same terms as everything else: an agent produced them over two days and they carry no more standing than a memory file or a state doc. CANON_AUDIT.md adjudicates other files and REVIEW_WORKLIST.md lists claims to check; neither is exempt. Nothing in the register outranks anything else in it by age, by title, or by being cited elsewhere

The corpus files' standing inside the register: user_turns*.jsonl / .md are intent — verbatim user turns, tool-extracted, spot-checked byte-identical against the source transcripts — and what needs reviewing there is the filter that produced them, not the prose inside them. Their caveat is the machine filter. git_record.md and desktop_docs_record.md are interpretation, agent-written reconstructions, and belong in the review pile

.claude/agents/ is committed, so a definition change is a diff both machines see, and the rest of .claude/ (settings.local.json and the legacy worktrees) stays ignored. These ten definitions — code-optimizer, critical-reviewer, eval-statistician, graph-refresher, logician, maths-algorithmist, order-of-operations, results-analyst, retrieval-scientist, v3-coder — are the surface that turns a written claim into an enforced rule

State docs sit in two places: five in-repo gitignored docs under docs/state/ (2026-07-20 v1 query-relative areas, 2026-07-22 retrieval literature sweep, 2026-07-22 v1 curve-walk facets and cluster-k, 2026-07-25 combine clusterk hybrid and judged eval usage burn, 2026-07-28 audit absorption full revert corroboration probe) and eleven flat on the OneDrive state-transfer\GRAG-Job folder, several of which are not mirrored into docs/state/ — including 2026-06-20 v3 contract vector arm, 2026-07-17 judge shootout, 2026-07-20 gold100 shipment, 2026-08-02 benchmark validity record, 2026-08-02 corpus facts, and a copy of USER_CANON.md

What the register does not cover, stated rather than omitted because the pile has to be complete to be a worklist: docs/handoff/ is empty — CLAUDE.md points at it as frozen historical handoffs and this working tree holds zero files there, unresolved; the live desktop memory directory is on the other machine, so section 6 lists the copy; v3/data/raw/Salesforce__HERB/README.md is presumed dataset-provided and was not opened because it sits inside the data quarantine; git history and commit messages are agent-written in places and are not enumerated; Claude Code transcripts are the source the corpus was extracted from, not documents to review; v3/ source code and its comments carry agent-written claims as well

The register's counts: 9 canon documents + the register itself, 6 raw records, 6 corpus files, 3 root docs, 6 v3 docs, 5 in-repo state docs, 11 OneDrive state docs, 25 live laptop memory files, 53 desktop memory copies, 32 laptop memory copies, 10 agent definitions, 3 other tree docs, 57 legacy worktree docs
